Definition: probably from G3007 (through the idea of destitution); a scarcity of food:--dearth, famine, hunger.
BiblicalUsage: limós means famine, hunger, and Scripture puts it to work in every part of life. In Acts 11:28, "and signified by the Spirit that there should be great dearth throughout all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar."; and in Luke 4:25, "when great famine was throughout all the land". In Luke 15:14, "there arose a mighty famine in that land"; and in 2 Corinthians 11:27, "in hunger and thirst".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe famine is God's loudest sermon on dependence — the widows of Elijah's day, the prodigal perishing with hunger, and Paul cold and naked. I hold that hunger drives men home: the prodigal remembered his father's bread, and that was the beginning of his return. My position is that when the famine comes, I will remember whose house has bread enough and to spare.
